data.long_meaning: Madhav means 'God of Love' and Rao is a title of respect for a ruler. So, Madhavrao means 'God of Love, Respected Ruler'. The name Madhavrao carries the meaning “God of Love” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Madhavrao usually hope their child will grow to embody god of love and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Madhavrao is a name that inspires love, compassion, and respect. It is believed to bring blessings of wealth, prosperity, and happiness in life.
data.etymology: Madhavrao belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Love.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Madhavrao total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Madhavrao has significant cultural relevance in the Hindu tradition, especially in the context of royal lineages. In southern India, in particular, the titled name Rao was commonly used by the ruling class as a mark of respect and loyalty to their monarchs. A name like Madhavrao signified aconnection to the divine through a powerful deity associated with love and sovereignty.
data.spiritual_significance: Madhavrao is deeply rooted in the spiritual tradition of Hinduism with Madhav being one of the many names of Lord Krishna, the divine embodiment of love and compassion. This name inspires the ideals of devotion, selflessness, and love towards the divine. The spiritual significance also extends beyond the individual possessing the name, for it serves as a constant reminder of the divine presence in our lives and the importance of cultivating an attitude of love and reverence.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Madhavrao is a name derived from the Sanskrit word 'Madhava', which means 'one who is intoxicated with love for Lord Krishna'. This name is believed to bestow the blessings of Lord Krishna and signifies deep devotion and spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Madhavrao was the ruling Maratha monarch of the Maratha Confederacy from 1760 to 1772. He came to power after the death of his father, Shahu Raje Bhonsle, who was a strong centraliser and had tried to merge the feudal Maratha territories into a single state under his rule. Madhavrao, however, was weak and indecisive and was easily manipulated by powerful feudal lords, leading to the dissolution of the Maratha Confederacy and the Peshwas gaining de facto power.

Madhavrao was the son of Shahu, the Maratha king of Satara. During his reign, the Maratha Empire suffered significant losses to the British East India Company. In 1773, the British took control of the strategically important port of Surat. Madhavrao's inability to prevent this loss further weakened his position and led to the increasing dominance of the Peshwas in Maratha internal affairs.
historical_references.context: Maratha Empire, British East India Company
